dedupe_keys.name: esa satellite constellation network emulator scne leo constellation routing and protocol simulation

description: The Satellite Constellation Network Emulator (SCNE) is an ESA project to build a simulation tool that assesses the protocol performance of new LEO telecommunication constellations, in particular routing protocols that affect end-to-end quality of service. It couples a commercial orbital simulator, STK, which designs constellations (orbits, satellite counts, altitudes, link budgets, antenna models), with an open-source network simulator, ns-3, that replays application traffic and protocols over generated traces; an orchestrator turns STK output into ns-3 configuration. Features listed are inter-satellite link routing (a global ideal reference algorithm is implemented), transport protocols, mobility management and configurable traffic models; the default scenario runs 24 hours with 288 satellites, 10 gateways and 50 user terminals. Producer: ESA Connectivity and Secure Communications, with Airbus D&S, Magister Solutions and VTT; the page says the final review was held on 1 July 2021. Coverage: generic LEO constellations, worldwide. Access: a project description page only; a download or repository was not found on it, so open_source is recorded as false, meaning no verified open-source release. Licence and cost: not stated, and running it needs a commercial STK licence with Professional and Communication modules. Caveats: the page describes a completed project, not a distributed product, and the simulation trades run-time performance against modelling accuracy. Simulation uses: it supports capacity planning and routing studies of satellite broadband and broadcast constellations. Related records: Ansys STK (platform-ansys-stk), the OpenSN emulation library (platform-opensn) and the Hypatia LEO simulator (model-hypatia).
